$\frac {\sqrt 2} 2 = \cos\left(\frac \pi 4\right) = \cos\left(2 \times \frac \pi 8\right) = 2\cos^2\left(\frac \pi 8\right) - 1$
Therefore $\cos^2\left(\frac \pi 8\right) = \frac 1 2\left(\frac {\sqrt 2} 2 + 1\right) = \frac {2 + \sqrt 2} 4$.

Since $\frac \pi 8 \in \left(0, \frac \pi 2\right)$, one has $\cos\left(\frac \pi 8\right) > 0$ and thus $\cos\left(\frac \pi 8\right) = \sqrt{\cos^2\left(\frac \pi 8\right)} = \frac {\sqrt{2 + \sqrt 2}} 2$.
